name: Can a backyard guest house have a kitchen in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: If a backyard guest house includes a kitchen, does it become something else in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: If a backyard guest house includes a kitchen, does it become something else in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Adding a kitchen is one of the biggest planning decisions in a backyard project. Once a kitchen is included, the unit is no longer just a casual guest space in practical terms; it is usually being designed as a separate dwelling. That means the project should account for plumbing, electrical load, ventilation, appliance clearances, storage, and circulation that support everyday use. It also affects the conversation with the design-build team because the structure should be laid out as a real living unit rather than a small auxiliary room. Homeowners should decide early whether they want a true living unit or a simplified guest suite, because changing that decision later can alter plans, costs, and approval expectations.
acceptedAnswer.description: In many cases, yes. A backyard guest house with a kitchen is typically treated as an ADU rather than a simple guest house. That changes the project scope, because the design now needs to support independent living, utility connections, and the permit path for a habitable unit.
